name: Think Systematically
definition: We build scalable processes with prompt feedback mechanisms. We take measures not only to fix defects, but also to prevent them in the future.

terms.label: build the system, not the fix

rows.situation: When the same defect appears twice
rows.under: Fixes it twice and moves on.
rows.justRight: Treats the repeat as the real defect and changes whatever let it through.
rows.over: Blocks all work until a perfect prevention exists for a defect that has cost almost nothing.

rows.situation: When the process only works because one person watches it
rows.under: Praises the person and leaves the process alone.
rows.justRight: Builds the check into the system so it holds when that person is on leave.
rows.over: Automates a process that runs three times a year and would have been cheaper by hand.

rows.situation: When a manual workaround is holding things together
rows.justRight: Counts what the workaround costs per unit of growth, then fixes the system before that cost compounds.
rows.over: Rips out the workaround before the replacement works, and breaks the operation.

rows.situation: When a defect takes weeks to surface
rows.under: Accepts the delay as the nature of the work.
rows.justRight: Shortens the loop so the signal comes back in hours, then actually uses it.
rows.over: Instruments everything and buries the team in alerts nobody reads.

rows.situation: When the volume is about to multiply
rows.under: Builds for today's volume and plans to revisit it later.
rows.justRight: Builds the version that holds at 10 times the volume, and knows where it breaks after that.
rows.over: Builds for a scale the business will not reach for years, and ships nothing this year.

rows.situation: When a case does not fit the process
rows.under: Handles it by hand every time and never tells anyone.
rows.justRight: Handles it, counts how often it happens, and folds it into the process when it stops being rare.
rows.over: Forces every exception through the process and gives the customer a worse answer to keep the system clean.
